# CDPM-Align (MICCAI 2026)

> CDPM-Align: Multi-Scale Guidance-Aligned Diffusion Pretraining for Robust Few-Shot Anatomical Landmark Detection. Roberto Di Via, Irina Voiculescu, Francesca Odone, Vito Paolo Pastore (MaLGa-DIBRIS, University of Genoa; Department of Computer Science, University of Oxford). MICCAI 2026, Springer LNCS.

CDPM-Align trains a class-conditional diffusion model with classifier-free guidance on small heterogeneous X-ray datasets and adds a multi-scale alignment loss that enforces directional consistency of the guidance signal across diffusion timesteps and UNet hierarchy levels (applied in the final 10% of pretraining). The pretrained UNet is fine-tuned end-to-end for landmark detection.

Key results (10- and 25-shot, Shenzhen chest / ISBI2015 cephalometric / DHA hand, 5 runs):
- Pretrained on only 988 unlabeled X-rays; best MRE in 5 of 6 dataset-budget settings.
- +22% on ISBI2015 10-shot (2.11 vs 2.70 mm), +42% on DHA 10-shot (2.51 vs 4.34 mm).
- Expected radial error below 1 mm at 25 shots on ISBI2015 (0.95 mm) and DHA (0.97 mm).
- Matches or surpasses a model pretrained on 112k NIH chest radiographs; self-supervised baselines collapse on heterogeneous data (20-25 mm MRE on DHA 10-shot).
